_about: Plural data for tools/check_vocab.mjs and docs/irregular_plurals.md. 'words' lists every CSV noun or adjective (all units) whose plural is irregular or worth a watch-out, with its plural RULE(S). The validator allows a plural only once all its rules are taught: lessons in content/lessons_1.1-1.6.json declare "teaches": ["plural:<rule>"]; rules first taught after 1.6 use ruleTaughtAt. Nouns not listed are classified automatically (pluralInfo in the validator); run `node tools/check_vocab.mjs --plurals` after adding CSV nouns: it fails if an irregular plural is missing here. 'adjectives' are adjectives without o/a whose (regular) plural the validator should generate. 'auto': true = listed for the doc only; the validator works the plural out itself.

rules.regular: vowel → + s (libro → libros); consonant → + es (capital → capitales, mes → meses)
rules.accent-loss: stressed last syllable ending in -n or -s loses its written accent (marrón → marrones, canción → canciones)
rules.accent-gain: -en with stress on the second-to-last syllable gains an accent (joven → jóvenes)
rules.unchanged: unstressed last syllable ending in -s: no change (el lunes → los lunes, el cumpleaños → los cumpleaños)
rules.compound: noun + de + noun: only the first noun changes (la hoja de papel → las hojas de papel)
rules.plural-only: always plural, even for one object (las tijeras, las gafas)
rules.mixed-masculine: a masculine plural covers a mixed group (los padres = mother and father)
rules.loanword: borrowed words ending in an unusual consonant add -s (el fan → los fans, el carnet → los carnets)
rules.el-feminine: feminine nouns starting with a stressed a take el in the singular only (el águila → las águilas)
rules.stressed-vowel: -í / -ú add -es or -s (none in the CSV yet)
rules.other: anything else (none in the CSV yet)
